extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans of Norm Macdonald, and researchers/archivists of comedy podcasts
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the format, production, episode structure, guest selection, distribution, and reception of the comedy talk podcast 'Norm Macdonald Live'. Useful for people studying or producing similar comedy/interview podcasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page classifies Norm Macdonald Live under the genres 'Comedy' and 'Talk', indicating expectations of comedic material and conversational/interview format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format: audio and video; talk show without studio audience; hour-long episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm Macdonald Live is a weekly audio and video podcast following a talk show format without a studio audience; each episode is approximately one hour in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect both audio-only and video editions; the absence of a live audience shapes pacing and performance (more conversational/intimate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode structure: opening remarks, guest interview, concluding 'Jokes' segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each hour-long episode features opening remarks between Macdonald and co-host Adam Eget (often involving elaborate comedic bits and irreverent chit-chat), leading into a guest interview, and concludes with a segment called 'Jokes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure implies three functional parts: host banter to set tone, substantive guest interview as the core content, and a finale of one-liners—useful model for pacing and segment planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Jokes' segment (one-liners from index cards)
rubrics_metrics.description: The show concludes with a segment called 'Jokes' in which the hosts and their guest take turns reading one-liners from index cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formalized closing gag segment that foregrounds concise joke-writing and performer delivery; practical for producing a predictable, repeatable finale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection: comedians, actors, entertainment community
rubrics_metrics.description: The show featured interviews with comedians, actors, and other members of the entertainment community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guest roster (e.g., Ray Romano, Adam Sandler, David Letterman, Jerry Seinfeld, Jim Carrey) signals emphasis on prominent entertainment figures and comedian peers as content drivers and audience draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production style and visual framing
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommencement of the third season featured a brand-new set as well as a new style of filming that seemed to prefer close-up camera shots on subjects rather than the traditional medium close-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual/production choices (set design, shot selection) affect tone and intimacy; closer framing increases conversational immediacy and changes viewer experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release schedule and seasons (weekly; hiatuses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a discontinued weekly audio and video podcast that ran for three seasons with gaps/hiatuses between seasons and episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular (weekly) cadence establishes audience expectation; hiatuses and irregular season lengths (e.g., 11, 13, then short third season) impact audience retention and archival practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution platforms and archival availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Launched by the Video Podcast Network and produced by Jash; distributed on YouTube, Amazon Prime, PlutoTV, with audio-only versions uploaded via iTunes. On February 16, 2018, archived episodes were taken off YouTube and then most major digital platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform choice affects discoverability and longevity; removal from major platforms is a risk to accessibility—important consideration for producers and archivists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specials and live-streamed event coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The show produced specials, such as live-streamed coverage of the US Masters golf tournament over several hours, featuring special call-in guests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including specials and live events diversifies content format (longform live streams, call-ins) and can engage niche audiences, but requires different production logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception qualities (reviewer-evaluated attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews described the show as 'smart, unpredictable, thought-provoking, and funny as hell' and 'a bit rough around the edges'; one reviewer called it 'the best podcast out there right now.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value wit, unpredictability, thoughtfulness, and humor, while noting production polish may be uneven; these attributes serve as evaluative criteria for quality in comedy podcasts.
